correctness.rationale: For each finite connected graph with positive masses and symmetric conductances, monotone φ_p(s)=|s|^(p−2)s yields a global C¹ gradient flow and comparison principle for differences of two solutions. Their vertex oscillation is nonincreasing; on complete G edge-Lipschitz L_G equals this oscillation. Any noncomplete connected G has an induced j−i−k path. Choose h_v=d_G(j,v) so h_i−h_j=1, h_k−h_i=1 and L_G(h)=1; perturb u−v=εh. For p>2 set background a_k=R, a_z=0 elsewhere, giving instantaneous edge-growth rate (p−1)c_ik R^(p−2)/m_i+o(1) as ε→0 then R→∞. For 1<p<2 set a_i=a_k=0, a_j=1 and all other background vertices distinct >3; the only zero gradient on edges incident to i/j is ik, giving c_ik ε^(p−2)/m_i+O(1)→∞. Since oriented edge ij is tight at time zero, positive derivative forces failure of two-input L_G nonexpansivity. p=2 is explicitly excluded from converse; one-input decay and fixed-positive-time infinite amplification are not claimed.
